name: Presentism
statement: Only the present exists; the past is gone and the future not yet real.
meaning: Presentism is the view in the metaphysics of time that only present things exist. The past and the future do not exist; only what exists now is real. On presentism there are no dinosaurs, since they existed but do not exist now, and no future Mars colonies, since they do not exist yet; the domain of what exists, absolutely and unrestrictedly, is exhausted by present things, and it constantly changes as time passes and new things come to be present while others cease. Presentism is primarily an ontological doctrine, a view about what exists, and it is naturally stated as the conjunction that only present things exist and that what is present changes. It contrasts with eternalism, on which past, present, and future entities all equally exist, the block universe, and now is a merely perspectival matter, and with the growing block theory, associated with C. D. Broad, on which the past and present exist but the future does not. Presentism is a form of the A-theory, the tensed theory of time, associated with the reality of temporal passage and an objective, moving present, and it takes tense and the present as metaphysically fundamental, in the spirit of McTaggart's A-series, which orders events as past, present, and future. It fits common sense and the experience of time as passing, but faces serious objections about truthmakers and special relativity.
mechanism: Presentism restricts the domain of existence to the present and lets that domain change with the passage of time. At any moment, what exists is exactly what exists now: the current arrangement of things. A moment later, the domain has changed; some things that were present are no longer, and new ones have come to be. This gives presentism its close fit with the tensed, A-theoretic picture of time, on which there is an objective distinction between past, present, and future and an objective flow or passage as the present moves along, in contrast to the eternalist block universe in which all times are equally real and passage is at best perspectival. Because only the present exists, presentism must handle talk that appears to concern the non-existent past and future by treating it as tensed: the sentence there were dinosaurs is true not because past dinosaurs exist to be spoken of, but in virtue of how things were, expressed by a past tense operator applied to present resources. This is where the theory is pressed hardest. The truthmaker or grounding problem asks what, in a world containing only present things, makes past-tensed truths true, since there is no present dinosaur and, for the presentist, no past dinosaur either to serve as truthmaker; presentists respond in various ways, appealing to present properties or traces, to tensed facts, or to denying that every truth needs a truthmaker. Cross-temporal relations pose a related difficulty, since a relation seems to require both relata to exist, yet we speak of present things standing in relations to past ones. And special relativity threatens the objective present that presentism needs.

examples.text: On presentism there are no dinosaurs, since they existed but do not exist now; only present things are real.
What exists is exactly what is present, and that domain constantly changes as new things become present and others cease.
There were dinosaurs is true in virtue of how things were, expressed by a past-tense operator, not by existing past things.

variants.name: The A-theory of time

whyItMatters: Presentism is one of the two leading positions in the metaphysics of time and the natural home of the intuition that time really passes. Its importance lies in taking seriously the manifest image of time: that the present is uniquely real and special, that the past is gone and the future open, and that there is an objective flow as now advances, features that eternalism's static block universe seems to deny. By making only the present exist, presentism offers an ontologically parsimonious picture that matches ordinary experience and the tensed structure of our language and thought about time. The debate between presentism and eternalism has organized the philosophy of time, forcing precision about tense, existence, and the reality of passage, and connecting to McTaggart's celebrated distinction between the A-series and the B-series. Presentism also sits at a fascinating collision between metaphysics and physics, since special relativity's relativity of simultaneity appears to deny the global, objective present that presentism requires, making the view a focal point for debates about how metaphysics should answer to science.

working.text: hold that the only things that exist are present things, and nothing past or future.
allow what exists to change as time passes, with the present objectively moving.
treat talk of the past and future as tensed claims about how things were or will be, not about existing entities.

limits: Presentism faces several serious objections. The truthmaker or grounding problem is the sharpest: if only present things exist, it is hard to see what makes past-tensed truths true, since there seems to be no present truthmaker for a claim like there were dinosaurs, and the past dinosaurs do not exist to serve either; presentists must appeal to present properties or traces, to primitive tensed facts, or to denying the truthmaker principle, and each response is disputed. The challenge from special relativity may be graver still: the relativity of simultaneity implies that there is no privileged, frame-independent present or global now, which appears to conflict with presentism's need for an objective present, so that presentism seems to require rejecting or reinterpreting well-confirmed physics. Cross-temporal relations are a further difficulty, since a relation between a present thing and a past one seems to require the past relatum to exist. Reference to and quantification over past individuals raise related worries. Some attributions and terms reward care: the growing block is associated with C. D. Broad and, earlier, Samuel Alexander, and parsimony as a motivation is standard but should be presented as such rather than as a settled advantage.
misreadings: Presentism is not the trivial claim that we are located in the present; it is the substantive ontological claim that only present things exist at all. It does not deny that there were dinosaurs or that there will be a future, only that past and future things exist now, and it grounds such truths in tense. And it is not obviously compatible with taking relativity at face value, since relativity challenges its objective present, so treating presentism as a truism about our location, as denying the reality of the past, or as untroubled by physics, misreads the view.
origin: The view in the metaphysics of time, a form of the tensed A-theory, that only present things exist, the past and future being unreal, contrasted with eternalism and the growing block and pressed by truthmaker and relativity objections.
